text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach for customer Mariner Bio (VPC: eu-west-1) on dedicated pool 'mariner-bios-pool'. p99=2.4s over last 15m (SLO 1.5s). Recent spike coincides with increased KV cache miss rate. Metrics: https://redwood.metrics/alerts/4032109999 :rotating_light:

jordan.ops: acked. I'm oncall and joining. grabbing logs now. :eyes:
maya-sre: pulling traces — looks like token generation tails on model-gpu-4 are spiking at tail latencies. p95 ~ 860ms, p99 ~ 2.3s.
liam-eng: any tenant attribution? can we see per-tenant concurrency?
sophie-cs: pinging Mariner Bio account team, FYI customer chat channel open. will update on impact and whether they're seeing errors on their side.
jordan.ops: run first quick checks: `redwoodctl pool status mariner-bios-pool --region eu-west-1`
liam-eng: output snippet: ```
pool: mariner-bios-pool
nodes: 6 (gpu-rtx-a6000)
avg_rps: 120
kv_cache_hit_rate: 68% -> falling
active_tenants: 12
hot_tenant: bio-ingest (rps 48, avg_token_length 1.8x baseline)
```
maya-sre: that bio-ingest tenant shows sustained short-chatty bursts. prefix cache isn't being used (requests are unique). could be high cold-start KV pressure.
jordan.ops: steps: 1) throttle offending tenant, 2) enable emergency fallback to compatible hosted model for that tenant, 3) add ephemeral nodes if needed. agree?
liam-eng: agree. propose throttle to 30% of baseline to reduce queuing and KV churn. command: ``redwoodctl tenant throttle --pool mariner-bios-pool --tenant bio-ingest --rate 30% --reason "SLO mitigation"``
jordan.ops: executing now.
incident-bot: command executed by jordan.ops at 4032110055.
sophie-cs: Mariner Bio engineering says they're ingesting a spike of small inference requests from automated QC pipeline and can pause for 10-15m if we ask. asking now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
liam-eng: while we wait for customer pause, enable fallback policy so requests from bio-ingest that exceed throttles are routed to `redwood-hosted-small` (lower-cost hosted variant) to preserve success rate. ``redwoodctl routing set-fallback --pool mariner-bios-pool --tenant bio-ingest --fallback-model redwood-hosted-small``
maya-sre: also increasing pool capacity by 1 node to relieve transient queuing: ``redwoodctl pool scale --pool mariner-bios-pool --delta 1``
jordan.ops: scaling request submitted (provisioning ~90s).
incident-bot: autoscaling event started for mariner-bios-pool at 4032110180; estimated ready 4032110270.
sophie-cs: Mariner Bio confirmed they can reduce QC pipeline to 20% in ~3 minutes.
liam-eng: good — throttle + fallback + customer pause should drop p99. monitoring.
maya-sre: telemetry after throttle+fallback (1m): p99 down to 1.1s, kv hit rate recovering to 82%, avg queue length reduced. :thumbsup:
jordan.ops: leaving a note: we opted not to evict tenant entirely because that would cause failed requests for them; fallback preserves availability. documented in thread.
vicente-se: from solutions perspective — recommend follow-up: 1) advise Mariner Bio to add client-side batching or private caching; 2) add tenant-level autoscaling policy for spikes; 3) we can provide a tenant QoS token to prevent future pool-wide SLO impacts. I'll draft recommendations.
sophie-cs: customer asked for an ETA on full recovery and whether we did any data-plane changes. responded: throttle + routing fallback + +1 node. they asked to be notified when we revert.
liam-eng: note: we created a short-lived routing override. command to revert: ``redwoodctl routing clear-fallback --pool mariner-bios-pool --tenant bio-ingest``
maya-sre: monitoring window 15m. p99 trend continuing downward. current p99=0.98s at 4032110400.
jordan.ops: preparing handoff to night NOC in 30m. who will own follow-up postmortem?
liam-eng: i'll own the technical writeup (root cause, KV cold misses, tenant patterns). sophie will coordinate customer-facing summary. jordan will do incident timeline.
sophie-cs: creating support ticket SB-4721 and linking to customer channel. will schedule customer debrief tomorrow.
incident-bot: paging reminder scheduled — handoff check-in at 4032111380.
jordan.ops: final checklist before handoff: - confirm p99 stable < 1.5s for 15m - remove emergency throttle if customer requests - document commands executed - file postmortem stub.
maya-sre: p99 stable at 0.9s for 10m and trending. kv hit rate 84%.
liam-eng: i've captured the diagnostics and saved kernel traces to `s3://redwood-logs/incidents/4032109999/` (log ids: 4032109999-kt1, 4032109999-rt2).
sophie-cs: customer confirmed they will resume QC at 25% and will coordinate changes to batching. thanked the team. :pray:
jordan.ops: handing off to NOC @maya-sre in 10m, please monitor and escalate if p99 > 1.5s again.
maya-sre: ack, monitoring. will escalate to eng if we see 2x baseline again.
jordan.ops: creating post-incident ticket and assigning to liam-eng. ticket: INC-4032109999.
liam-eng: will open RCA doc and link to support ticket.
sophie-cs: thanks all. closing active war room. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: incident summary (auto): detection: p99 > SLO (4032109999), mitigation: tenant throttle + fallback routing + +1 node, outcome: p99 recovered to <1.5s within 7m, customer impact: degraded latency for Mariner Bio briefly, no request failures (fallback preserved success). Hand-off: NOC monitoring until 4032111400.
jordan.ops: thread closed for active mitigation. follow-up items assigned.
